blindSummary: Local character: conservative, semi-urban, with no documented subnational variation in LGBT policy or enforcement. The national dossier located no state/province-specific trans ordinance, incident series or enforcement finding for this division; all three sources below are national-context legal and survey material that applies across the country. A trans visitor's risk picture therefore rests on the national framework plus this local climate.
blindSourceSummaries: National newspaper (22 July 2024): the capital's central district court ruled that a police officer's advice to an LGBTQ+ individual midway through legal gender change to "avoid using public restrooms for a while" infringed their personal rights; the court awarded 10% of the damages claimed, final 2 July. Both first and second instances ruled for the plaintiff; the appellate court called comfortable restroom use "a fundamental and universal human right", and the officer received human-rights education from the national human-rights commission. Also cites the commission's 2021 survey of 591 trans respondents (41% had used a restroom of a different gender than their identity out of fear; 39% avoided food and drinks; 36% forwent restroom use) and a 2021 ruling in a mid-sized industrial city awarding damages against an academy operator who barred a trans student from using restrooms.

NOTE: page body did not load at fetch time (navigation chrome only); the underlying national wire-service article (8 May 2024, tagged "legal sex change" / "transgender surgery") headlines a court ruling against mandating transgender surgery to change legal sex status — the national framework barring surgical requirements for legal gender recognition.

National daily (21 March 2024): a youth LGBTQ+ organisation presented research on school safety for trans students (survey of 86 trans/genderqueer students, 24 Sept-7 Oct 2023): 59 of 86 (69%) felt uncomfortable using school restrooms, with respondents describing avoiding drinking water, waiting for empty stalls and leaving early; proposes amendments to the educational-facilities safety act, school health act and school-violence prevention act for inclusive facilities. Also covers a major-city study (January 2024, 208 LGBTQ students surveyed): 39% reported mistreatment such as outing, insults and violence at school because of gender identity or sexual orientation.
